title: Trump Calls Iran Ceasefire 'On Life Support' After Rejecting Deal
excerpt: President dismisses Tehran's counteroffer as a 'piece of garbage,' putting a fragile month-old truce on the brink of collapse.
body:
President Donald Trump declared Monday that the U.S.-Iran ceasefire is 'on massive life support' after he refused to accept Tehran's counteroffer to an American peace proposal, using some of his sharpest language yet to describe the breakdown in diplomacy.

**What happened:**
Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump said he could not even finish reading Iran's response. 'After reading that piece of garbage they sent us — I didn't even finish reading it,' he said, calling the state of the ceasefire 'unbelievably weak.' He had already signaled his displeasure on Sunday, posting on Truth Social that Tehran's reply was 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE.' Iran, in turn, accused Washington of making 'unreasonable' and 'excessive demands,' while insisting it asked only for its 'legitimate rights.'

**Why this matters:**
Iran's counteroffer reportedly demanded war reparations, recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, an end to U.S. sanctions, and the return of frozen assets — terms Washington has shown no appetite to accept. The month-old truce, which began on April 8 and was unilaterally extended by Trump on April 21, has been fragile from day one, with both sides accusing each other of violations. The breakdown is already rattling global energy markets, with Brent Crude climbing toward $104 a barrel as the Strait of Hormuz — a chokepoint for roughly 20 percent of global oil supply — remains effectively paralyzed.

**What to watch:**
Trump travels to Beijing later this week, where he is expected to press President Xi Jinping to use China's economic leverage over Tehran to push Iran back toward the negotiating table.
nri_angle: With Brent Crude surging past $104 a barrel and the Strait of Hormuz still choked, Indian-Americans with ties to India — the world's third-largest oil importer — should watch closely as rising energy prices could squeeze household budgets and rattle the Indian economy.
